newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong activists protest against freedom curbs.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong activists protest against freedom curbs.

text.p: Pro-democracy activists handed in a protest note and staged a small but noisy demonstration on Thursday outside the office of Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa, denouncing his plan to curb civil liberties.

Led by legislator Fred Li, a dozen or so protesters brandished placards and shouted slogans on the doorstep of the financial district building where Tung has his offices after police stopped them from entering the lobby.
"Defend the right to demonstrate", "Defend the right to form organisations", they chanted as policemen looked on.
On Wednesday Tung launched plans to curb public demonstrations and foreign funding for political groups in Hong Kong after the British colony of over 150 years reverts to China on July 1.
Tung's move was widely expected after China resolved in February to repeal several existing Hong Kong laws protecting civil liberties and political rights.

Under the plan, societies and political parties would have to be registered, and their registration could be refused if they are known to have ties to or receive funds from foreign political organisations or individuals. People wishing to hold demonstrations would also need permission from police.

Li, a member of the popular Democratic Party, told Reuters he hoped Tung would think twice. "Mr Tung should really consider, and he should explain to the world ... all these (plans) are really unnecessary.
"Now they want us to seek permission to demonstrate. That is really against human rights," Li said.
An aide from Tung's office accepted a note from the group.
